root_cause: Table.add_row auto-creates missing columns with Column(_index=index); Column.highlight defaults to False, so a Table(highlight=True) built without add_column never highlights cells in those implicit columns.
best_solution: In Table.add_row, where a new column is created because the row has more cells than columns (`if index == len(columns): column = Column(_index=index)`), pass the table's setting: `Column(_index=index, highlight=self.highlight)`. The statement says exactly this: Column.highlight defaults to False, so columns added by add_row should default to Table.highlight. add_column already inherits table-level settings, so the implicit path was the only one that dropped it.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that makes implicitly created columns carry highlight=self.highlight (e.g. setting column.highlight after construction). The hidden test checks both the attribute (table.columns[i].highlight == table.highlight) and the rendered ANSI output, so render-time-only fixes that leave Column.highlight False would fail the attribute assertion.
hidden_test_demands:
tests/test_table.py::test_columns_highlight_added_by_add_row: Table(show_header=False, highlight=True).add_row('1', repr('FOO')); asserts columns[0].highlight and columns[1].highlight == table.highlight, and Console(record=True) export_text(styles=True) == '┌───┬───────┐
│ \x1b[1;36m1\x1b[0m │ \x1b[32m'FOO'\x1b[0m │
└───┴───────┘
' (repr highlighter: number bold cyan, string green).
locating_signals: Title 'fix(table): highlight columns added by add_row' names the module (table) and the method (add_row); description names Column.highlight and Table.highlight. grep 'Column(' inside add_row gives the single line to change. Gold function named directly.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6, v7 passed with a patch byte-identical to gold (529 chars, 12-29 tool calls, 41-55 s). v8 failed with an empty patch after 14 tool calls / 17 s: it read the whole of rich/table.py several times in chunks plus the whole tests/test_table.py, and the prompt hit 28,673 input tokens + 4,096 output, over the 32,768-token context window (litellm ContextWindowExceededError after 5 retries). It had already located the exact line; the failure was context budget, not reasoning.
generalizable_lesson: For a one-line fix the statement already localizes (module + method named), grep for the construction site and read only a narrow window around it; never read whole large source or test files into a 32k-context model. Keep a hard token budget on tool outputs (truncate file reads, head test files) and commit the edit as soon as the target line is found, since a context overflow yields an empty patch even when the location is known. Separately: when a child object (column, field, option) is created implicitly, it should inherit the parent's defaults the same way the explicit add_* path does.
